action: Monitor serum digoxin concentration targeting 0.5 to less than 0.9 ng/mL
action_detail: Digoxin dose should be individualized to achieve serum digoxin concentration 0.5-<0.9 ng/mL. Risk of death is independently associated with serum digoxin concentration, with significantly higher risk at concentrations >=1.2 ng/mL and >=1.6 ng/mL.
source_text: Individualized variable dose to achieve serum digoxin concentration 0.5-<0.9 ng/mL. Risk of death independently associated with serum digoxin concentration >=1.2 ng/mL and >=1.6 ng/mL (COR 2b, LOE B-R)

action: Monitor renal function when prescribing digoxin
action_detail: Low doses (0.125 mg daily or every other day) should be used initially if the patient has impaired renal function. Renal function affects digoxin clearance and serum concentration.
source_text: Low doses (0.125 mg daily or every other day) should be used initially if the patient has impaired renal function. Higher doses are rarely used or needed in the management of patients with HF.

action_detail: Digoxin is usually initiated at a low dose (0.125-0.25 mg daily) because higher doses are rarely required and are potentially detrimental. Low doses (0.125 mg daily or every other day) should be used if patient is >70 years of age, has impaired renal function, or has low lean body mass. Higher doses (0.375-0.50 mg daily) are rarely used or needed.

properties.low_dose: 0.125 mg daily or every other day

source_text: Therapy with digoxin is commonly initiated and maintained at a dose of 0.125 to 0.25 mg daily. Low doses (0.125 mg daily or every other day) should be used initially if the patient is >70 years of age (COR 2b, LOE B-R)

action: Reduce digoxin dose in elderly patients over 70 years
action_detail: Low doses of digoxin (0.125 mg daily or every other day) should be used initially if the patient is >70 years of age. Higher doses (0.375-0.50 mg daily) are rarely used or needed.

properties.dose_adjustment: 0.125 mg daily or every other day for age >70

source_text: Low doses (0.125 mg daily or every other day) should be used initially if the patient is >70 years of age, has impaired renal function, or has a low lean body mass.

action: Avoid serum digoxin concentrations at or above 1.2 ng/mL
action_detail: Retrospective analyses of large-scale clinical trials showed a linear relationship between mortality and digoxin serum concentration. Risk of death was significantly higher at concentrations >=1.2 ng/mL and >=1.6 ng/mL. Digoxin should be dosed to maintain serum concentration 0.5-<0.9 ng/mL.
source_text: Risk of death was independently associated with serum digoxin concentration, with a significantly higher risk observed in those with concentrations >=1.2 ng/mL and >=1.6 ng/mL.

action_detail: Clinical worsening after withdrawal of digoxin has been shown. Therapy with digoxin may either be continued in the absence of a contraindication or discontinued with caution. Avoid abrupt discontinuation.
source_text: Clinical worsening after withdrawal of digoxin has been shown. Therapy with digoxin may either be continued in the absence of a contraindication or discontinued with caution.

action: Consider digoxin for symptomatic HFrEF patients despite GDMT
action_detail: In patients with symptomatic HFrEF despite GDMT (or who are unable to tolerate GDMT), digoxin might be considered to decrease hospitalizations for HF. GDMT is expected to be optimized before considering the addition of digoxin.
source_text: In patients with symptomatic HFrEF despite GDMT (or who are unable to tolerate GDMT), digoxin might be considered to decrease hospitalizations for HF (COR 2b, LOE B-R)
